rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A participle after a noun may be an agreeing adjective or an accusative predicate attached to the implicit noun after معه or عنده; its intended attachment determines the case.
rows.anchor: على الرجل وحملته على الاسم المضمر المعروف نصبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the construction with the horse riding a mule, the participle cannot be an adjective; it is only a predicate in the accusative.
rows.anchor: لا يكون فيه وصف ولا يكون إلا خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For paired, enduring qualities, adjective agreement is stronger; accusative is possible but suggests a temporary state rather than two coequal traits.
rows.anchor: هذا رجل عاقل لبيب لم يجعل الآخر حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh rejects the proposed inverted-order analysis (qalb), since it gives the wrong case and fails on the cited adjective constructions.
rows.anchor: لو كان هذا على القلب كما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With a participle describing the vocative, an overt agent such as Zayd cannot be attached as its adjective; an agent like the addressee’s father can be construed separately, and pronoun placement affects case.
rows.anchor: الواطئها زيد من قبل أن الواطئها من صفة المنادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In rab rajul wa-akhīhi, the genitive brother is understood as an indefinite brother belonging to a man; this construction is weak and requires an indefinite to precede it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز لك أن تقول رب اخيه حتى تكون قد ذكرت قبل ذلك نكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the line “أي فتى هيجاء أنت وجارها,” جارها must be genitive: the poet praises the war’s young man and its neighbor, not a specific man joined in the praise.
rows.anchor: إلا الجر لأنه لا يريد أن يجعله جار شيء آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s couplet about dunes and their ridges is cited as poetic evidence for the unusual genitive coordination in rab rajul wa-akhīhi.
rows.anchor: هذا حجة لقوله رب رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A supplementary description may follow the first noun as an agreeing adjective, or be detached and started as a nominative sentence; accusative praise is another construction.
rows.anchor: الصفة فإن كثيرا من العرب يجعلونه صفة فيتبعونه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur’an 4:162, المقيمين الصلاة is accusative, while المؤتون الزكاة is treated as a new nominative phrase; making the whole sequence nominative would also be sound.
rows.anchor: من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qur’an 2:177, الصابرين may be accusative like the praise construction above, or nominative as a fresh beginning.
rows.anchor: ولو ابتدأته فرفعته على الابتداء كان جيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic examples show that the following epithet can agree with the first noun or restart independently; al-Kharnq’s الطيبون parallels المؤتون, while Ibn Khayyat illustrates a new nominative phrase.
rows.anchor: ومثل هذا فى الابتداء قول ابن خياط العكلى

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus reports Arabic usage with both nominative and accusative epithets, including النازلون ... والطيبين and الظاعنون ... والقائلين; he also permits genitive coordination in مررت بزيد أخيك وصاحبك, citing a rajaz line.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس أن من العرب من يقول النازلون بكل معترك والطيبين

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: Isa reports hearing Dhu al-Rumma recite the cited descriptive phrase in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وزعم عيسى أنه سمع ذا الرمة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil analyzes accusative praise as an unspoken verb such as “I mention,” used when the audience already knows the fact; the verb is not normally made explicit, as in boastful tribal declarations.
rows.anchor: الخليل أن نصب هذا على أنك

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: A derogatory supplementary description such as “شعثا” can be accusative through an unspoken “I mention them,” though it may instead be attached as a genitive adjective.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل كأنه قال وأذكرهن شعثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise requires a fitting description and a listener able to recognize its subject; not every person or quality can bear the same exalted praise, and divine honor language does not transfer unchanged to people.
rows.anchor: كل موضع يجوز فيه التعظيم ولا كل صفة يحسن أن يعظم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speaker may identify someone through an added name as though the listener had asked who the person was, even when no question was spoken.
rows.anchor: كما قال مررت برجل زيد فتنزله منزلة من قال لك من هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading of امرأته حمالة الحطب is an insult formed with an omitted verb such as “I mention”; it does not repeat Zayd’s name or introduce unknown information.
rows.anchor: لم يجعل الحمالة خبرا للمرأة ولكنه كأنه قال أذكر حمالة الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insults can use facts already known to the listener: ʿUrwa’s “عداة الله من كذب وزور” and al-Nābigha’s “وجوه قرود” exemplify abusive descriptions.
rows.anchor: وجوه قرود تبتغي من تجادع

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus reports hearing al-Farazdaq recite the aunt-and-aunt poem as an insult; Sībawayh also says the nominative continuation is valid Arabic.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس أنه سمع الفرزدق ينشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sībawayh says Hassān’s comparison of the people’s bodies and minds enumerates their traits rather than insulting them.
rows.anchor: أن يجعله شتما ولكنه أراد أن يعدد صفاتهم ويفسرها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil allows the same Hassān phrase to be construed as an insult, with its epithet accusative under an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل رحمه الله لو جعله شتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accusative modifier can simply identify someone, without praise or blame: محصن is named with an explicit “I mean” verb, not an omitted boast or insult.
rows.anchor: فنصبه على أعني وهو فعل يظهر لأنه لم يرد

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: In expressions of compassion, المسكين may be a genitive appositive, an accusative object of an understood verb, or a nominative fresh comment; the poet’s البائسا supplies an example.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه الله أنه يقول

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus argues merciful epithets simply match the preceding syntax and rejects an omitted noun for nominative examples; Sībawayh attributes that raised analysis to al-Khalil and Ibn Abi Ishaq.
rows.anchor: وأما يونس فزعم أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khalil’s construction إنه المسكين أحمق inserts a nominative epithet between subject and predicate, but Sībawayh calls this analysis weak.
rows.anchor: إنه المسكين أحمق على الإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When المسكين refers to the speaker or addressee, it cannot be an appositive that leaves the referent uncertain; use the accusative construction or a fresh nominative instead.
rows.anchor: فلا يحسن فيه البدل لأنك إذا عنيت المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two accepted constructions for compassionate naming express the same meaning despite differing in form.
rows.anchor: المعنى واحد كما اختلف اللفظان
